# Every setting and its default

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen_variable_reference.py from roles/*/defaults/main.yml. Do not edit by hand:
     change the comment in the role's defaults file and run the script. -->

This page lists **every setting a role reads**, with the value it has when you set nothing, and
what the role's own comment says. It is generated from `roles/<role>/defaults/main.yml`, so it is
never out of date. Where to put a setting, and which place wins when it is in two, is in
[VARIABLES.md](VARIABLES.md). Values are shortened to one line here: the role file has the full one.

A setting that is a list (`[a, b]`) **replaces** the default list when you set it; it does not add
to it. Repeat the entries you want to keep.

## aap_ee

File: `roles/aap_ee/defaults/main.yml`

> SET THE EXECUTION ENVIRONMENT (playbooks/aap_ee.yml): puts one execution environment on many job templates at once, through AAP's API - after you add a new EE to AAP (docs/EXECUTION_ENVIRONMENT.md, chapter 6). Run it with Check first: it lists every template it would change, from which EE to which. A rebuild pushed with the next tag: aap_ee_image gives the EE that image (or change its Image in AAP by hand), and every template on it follows.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `aap_ee_name` | (empty) | The execution environment to put on the templates: its name in AAP (Automation Execution > Infrastructure > Execution Environments), or its ID when two have that name. |
| `aap_ee_image` | (empty) | Its new Image (registry/name:tag): a rebuild's next tag, pushed - every job template on this EE then runs it; none need be picked below. The image it has now is refused (an execution node that has a tag keeps it). "" = as it is. |
| `aap_ee_project` | (empty) | Which job templates (at least one of the three, or only aap_ee_image; never every template in AAP): the templates of this AAP project (its name): your site-automation project |
| `aap_ee_from` | `[]` | Only the templates on one of these execution environments now (names or IDs); none = those with no execution environment set, which use the project's or organization's default (left as they are otherwise). Empty = any. |
| `aap_ee_templates` | `[]` | more job templates, by name or ID - whatever they are on |
| `aap_ee_exclude` | `[]` | templates left out, by name or ID (jobs that stay on another EE) |
| `aap_ee_ca_path` | (empty) | a CA file for AAP's HTTPS certificate ("" = what the execution environment trusts) |

## aap_email_question

File: `roles/aap_email_question/defaults/main.yml`

> THE "ALSO EMAIL THE REPORT TO" QUESTION (playbooks/aap_email_question.yml): adds a text box to the survey of every report template and of the workflows that run them, through AAP's API, so whoever launches one can send that run's report to more people (report_email_also, added to the template's report_email_to). Run it once, and again after you add report templates. docs/EMAIL_REPORTS.md, "Also email the report to".

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `aap_email_question_state` | `present` | present = add the question; absent = take it out again |
| `aap_email_question_playbooks` | `- aap_health_check.yml - aap_template_audit.yml - tenable_scan.yml - act_fix_approved.yml…` | Which templates: the job templates whose playbook is one of these (the file name - your template names do not matter). Every playbook that can email a report is here; a test keeps the list complete. |
| `aap_email_question_templates` | `[]` | more job templates or workflows, by name or ID |
| `aap_email_question_exclude` | `[]` | templates left out, by name or ID |
| `aap_email_question_workflows` | `true` | also the workflows that run them (a job in a workflow is never asked its own survey) |
| `aap_email_question_project` | (empty) | only job templates of this AAP project (its name); empty = any project |
| `aap_email_question_ca_path` | (empty) | a CA file for AAP's HTTPS certificate ("" = what the execution environment trusts) |
| `aap_email_question_text` | `Also email the report to` | The question, as whoever launches a template sees it. A text box of several lines (a pasted list keeps its line breaks), not required, empty by default. |
| `aap_email_question_description` | (worked out by the role; see its file) | The help text under the question. |

## aap_health

File: `roles/aap_health/defaults/main.yml`

> AAP HEALTH CHECK (playbooks/aap_health_check.yml): a read-only look at a containerized AAP 2.5+ host - the OS, the rootless containers and their systemd user units, the logs, the controller's database, the controller and gateway API, receptor and the certificates. Every check gives PASS, WARN or FAIL with a detail and a hint; an HTML and a JSON report are written on the host. Nothing is restarted, changed or installed. docs/AAP_HEALTH_CHECK.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `aap_health_user` | `ansible` | The account the AAP containers run as (rootless podman, systemd --user units). |
| `aap_health_inventory_file` | (empty) | The installer's inventory file (DB name and user, certificate paths are read from it). Empty = found by name (aap_health_inventory_name) in that account's home, at most aap_health_inventory_depth folders down. |
| `aap_health_inventory_name` | `inventory-growth` | the installer inventory file name looked for |
| `aap_health_inventory_depth` | `2` | how many folders down from the home it is looked for |
| `aap_health_unit_regex` | `'^(automation-.*\|postgresql.*\|redis.*\|receptor.*)\.service$'` | The systemd user units that make up AAP (each runs the container of its name, or the --name in the unit). |
| `aap_health_cmd_timeout` | `60` | seconds any one command may take (podman, psql, ausearch...) before it is given up |
| `aap_url` | `https://localhost` | Controller and gateway API. aap_username / aap_password: vault them, or attach a "Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform" credential (its CONTROLLER_USERNAME / CONTROLLER_PASSWORD are read). The calls are made from the AAP host. |
| `aap_username` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'CONTROLLER_USERNAME') or lookup('ansible.builtin.env',…` | the API login (an AAP administrator or auditor); vault it |
| `aap_password` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'CONTROLLER_PASSWORD') or lookup('ansible.builtin.env',…` | its password; vault it |
| `aap_token` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'CONTROLLER_OAUTH_TOKEN') or lookup('ansible.builtin.en…` | an API token instead of the username and password (sent as a Bearer token) |
| `aap_health_validate_certs` | `false` | Check the gateway's HTTPS certificate. Its own setting, not aap_validate_certs: an AAP credential on the template sets that one (its "Verify SSL"), and a certificate never names localhost - with aap_url https://localhost it can only fail. |
| `aap_health_api_timeout` | `60` | seconds for one API call |
| `aap_health_api_slow_s` | `5` | an inventory's hosts/?page_size=100 slower than this (or not 200): FAIL |
| `aap_health_api_time_inventories` | `[]` | inventory IDs whose hosts page is timed; [] = every inventory (up to aap_health_api_time_max) |
| `aap_health_api_time_max` | `50` | inventories timed at most |
| `aap_health_focus_inventories` | `[]` | inventory IDs always reported (db and api), even when fine, e.g. [8] |
| `aap_health_api_light_warn_s` | `1.0` | the smallest requests (ping, me, config) slower than this: WARN |
| `aap_health_api_light_fail_s` | `5.0` | slower than this (or not 200): FAIL |
| `aap_health_stuck_minutes` | `15` | pending or waiting longer: FAIL |
| `aap_health_running_hours` | `4` | running longer: WARN |
| `aap_health_cleanup_max_days` | `8` | a cleanup system job (activity stream, job details) not run for longer: WARN |
| `aap_health_capacity_warn_pct` | `10` | an instance with less capacity left: WARN |
| `aap_health_last_seen_minutes` | `10` | an instance not seen for longer: WARN |
| `aap_health_mem_warn_mb` | `2048` | OS MemAvailable below: WARN |
| `aap_health_mem_fail_mb` | `1024` | below: FAIL |
| `aap_health_swap_warn_pct` | `25` | swap used at or above: WARN |
| `aap_health_swap_fail_pct` | `75` | at or above: FAIL |
| `aap_health_load_warn` | `1.0` | 5-minute load per CPU |
| `aap_health_load_fail` | `2.0` | at or above: FAIL |
| `aap_health_disk_warn_pct` | `80` | space and inodes |
| `aap_health_disk_fail_pct` | `90` | at or above: FAIL |
| `aap_health_disk_paths` | `[/, /home, /var, /tmp]` | also the podman storage and the postgres data folder, found on the host |
| `aap_health_time_warn_s` | `1.0` | clock offset (chronyc tracking) |
| `aap_health_time_fail_s` | `5.0` | at or above (or not synchronised): FAIL |
| `aap_health_selinux_users_ok` | `[unconfined_u, staff_u, sysadm_u]` | SELinux users rootless podman works as |
| `aap_health_dnf_recent_days` | `7` | a dnf transaction this recent, and fapolicyd denials today: WARN |
| `aap_health_fapolicyd_required` | `false` | fapolicyd not running: INFO; true (a site that must run it) = FAIL |
| `aap_health_fqdn` | (empty) | the host's name to resolve; empty = hostname -f |
| `aap_health_container_mem_warn_mb` | `4096` | Containers one container using more: WARN |
| `aap_health_container_mem_fail_mb` | `8192` | one container using more: FAIL |
| `aap_health_min_uptime_minutes` | `10` | a container up for less: WARN (restarted?) |
| `aap_health_restart_warn` | `3` | restarts (podman or systemd) at or above: WARN |
| `aap_health_dangling_warn` | `10` | dangling images or volumes at or above: WARN |
| `aap_health_log_since` | `2h` | Logs podman logs --since (2h, 30m, 1d) |
| `aap_health_log_proxy_max_lines` | `50000` | gateway proxy lines read at most (the last ones) |
| `aap_health_log_match_max` | `2000` | matching lines kept per container at most |
| `aap_health_envoy_regex` | (empty) | the proxy's access-log line, if not Envoy's default or JSON: named groups path, code, dur, up |
| `aap_health_slow_ms` | `5000` | a proxied request slower than this (upstream time): listed |
| `aap_health_slow_max` | `15` | slowest requests listed |
| `aap_health_5xx_fail` | `20` | 5xx responses in the window at or above: FAIL (any: WARN) |
| `aap_health_log_web_patterns` | `HARAKIRI: HARAKIRI worker killed: worker [0-9]+ killed\|killed.*worker\|SIGKILL\|signal 9 Tr…` | controller-web: name -> regex (case counts; awk-compatible) |
| `aap_health_log_web_fail` | `[HARAKIRI, worker killed]` | any of these: FAIL (others: WARN; a worker uWSGI only recycled: INFO) |
| `aap_health_log_task_patterns` | `dispatcher error: "(ERROR\|Exception).*dispatch\|dispatch.*(ERROR\|Exception)" callback rece…` | controller-task: name -> regex (all: WARN) |
| `aap_health_log_other_patterns` | `Traceback: Traceback ERROR: '\[ERROR\]\| ERROR \|^ERROR\|level=error'` | the gateway, hub and EDA containers: lines logged at level ERROR, Tracebacks |
| `aap_health_proxy_match` | `gateway-proxy` | container names (regex) of the gateway proxy, controller web and task |
| `aap_health_web_match` | `controller-web` | the controller web container |
| `aap_health_task_match` | `controller-task` | the controller task container |
| `aap_health_other_log_match` | `'^automation-(gateway\|hub\|eda)'` | the containers whose Tracebacks and ERRORs are counted |
| `aap_health_log_context_lines` | `5` | lines kept after each matching line (an ERROR's message is often on the next lines) |
| `aap_health_log_error_groups` | `5` | the containers' ERRORs grouped by message: this many listed, with counts |
| `aap_health_log_oom_journal` | `true` | as root (become; quietly skipped without it): the kernel's OOM kills in the last 2 h |
| `aap_health_log_oom_match` | `uwsgi` | an OOM-killed process matching this (regex) makes controller-web FAIL |
| `aap_health_pg_container` | (empty) | Database (podman exec into the postgres container; peer login, else the installer inventory's controller_pg_password) empty = the container whose name matches aap_health_pg_match |
| `aap_health_pg_match` | `postgres` | the postgres container's name (regex) |
| `aap_health_pg_data_dest` | `/var/lib/pgsql/data` | the data folder inside the container (its host folder is found from the mount) |
| `aap_health_db_statement_timeout` | `120` | seconds per query |
| `aap_health_db_vars_avg_warn_kb` | `10` | host variables per inventory: average / largest host |
| `aap_health_db_vars_avg_fail_kb` | `50` | average above: FAIL |
| `aap_health_db_vars_max_warn_kb` | `100` | the largest host above: WARN |
| `aap_health_db_vars_max_fail_kb` | `500` | above: FAIL |
| `aap_health_db_host_jobs_warn` | `5000` | job host summaries of one host above (the Hosts list reads each host's recent jobs): WARN |
| `aap_health_db_host_groups_warn` | `100` | groups one host is in, above: WARN (an inventory source's keyed groups can put a host in hundreds) |
| `aap_health_db_dead_min` | `10000` | a table with more dead rows than this (and 20% of its live ones): WARN (autovacuum behind) |
| `aap_health_db_facts_avg_warn_kb` | `100` | ansible_facts per host, average |
| `aap_health_db_size_warn_gb` | `50` | the database larger: WARN |
| `aap_health_db_conn_warn_pct` | `80` | of max_connections |
| `aap_health_db_conn_fail_pct` | `95` | at or above: FAIL |
| `aap_health_db_long_s` | `30` | a query running longer: WARN (aap_health_db_long_fail_s: FAIL) |
| `aap_health_db_long_fail_s` | `300` | a query running longer: FAIL |
| `aap_health_db_idle_tx_s` | `60` | idle in transaction longer: WARN |
| `aap_health_db_jobevent_warn` | `20000000` | job event rows (estimate) above: WARN |
| `aap_health_db_job_keep_days` | `130` | the oldest job older than this: WARN (Cleanup Job Details keeps 120 days by default) |
| `aap_health_receptor_container` | (empty) | Receptor empty = the container whose name matches aap_health_receptor_match |
| `aap_health_receptor_match` | `receptor` | the receptor container's name (regex) |
| `aap_health_receptorctl_containers` | `[]` | where receptorctl is run (the first that has it); [] = the receptor container, then controller task and web |
| `aap_health_receptor_socket` | (empty) | empty = read from the container's receptor.conf (control-service filename) |

| `aap_health_cert_files` | `[]` | more certificate files on the AAP host (full paths) |
| `aap_health_cert_warn_days` | `30` | expires in fewer days: WARN |
| `aap_health_cert_fail_days` | `7` | in fewer days (or expired): FAIL |
| `aap_health_trust_cas` | `[DoD Root CA 3, DoD Root CA 4, DoD Root CA 5, DoD Root CA 6]` | labels that must be in the system trust store; [] = not checked |
| `aap_health_report_dir` | (empty) | Output on the AAP host; empty = <the AAP account's home>/aap-health |
| `aap_health_top` | `10` | top offenders listed per check |
| `aap_health_email` | `true` | Email the report like the other reports: to report_email_to, through the mail relay in all.yml (report_email_from, report_email_smtp_host ...; docs/EMAIL_REPORTS.md) - FAIL and WARN first, then every area, the sortable HTML attached. Nothing is sent while report_email_to is empty. false = never emailed (the launch box… (all of it: the role file) |
| `aap_health_web` | `true` | Put the report on the report website as well (report_web_dest in all.yml, like the other reports; docs/WEB_REPORTS.md): FAIL and WARN first, then every area. Nothing happens while report_web_dest is empty. false = never on the website. |

## aap_template_audit

File: `roles/aap_template_audit/defaults/main.yml`

> AAP - TEMPLATE VARIABLES AUDIT (playbooks/aap_template_audit.yml): reads every job template and workflow template through AAP's API and says which settings in their Variables box belong somewhere else - connection settings, addresses, site-wide settings, one set the same way in many templates, secrets (their names only, never their values) - and where. Read-only. docs/TEMPLATE_AUDIT.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `aap_template_audit_project` | (empty) | Which templates: every job template and workflow the AAP user can see, or these narrowed only the job templates of this AAP project (its name); workflows are all read |
| `aap_template_audit_workflows` | `true` | read the workflow templates too (false = the job templates only) |
| `aap_template_audit_exclude` | `[]` | templates left out, by name or ID |
| `aap_template_audit_repeat_min` | `3` | A setting with the same value in this many templates or more is flagged: one change would have to be made in each (0 = never) |
| `aap_template_audit_site_wide_roles` | `[site_email, site_act, site_findings]` | Site-wide: the settings of these roles are the ones "usually in all.yml" (as aap/extra_vars marks them), read from their defaults when the job runs - and these more |
| `aap_template_audit_site_wide` | `[]` | more site-wide settings, by name |
| `aap_template_audit_per_enclave` | `[]` | Settings that differ by enclave: each enclave has its own AAP, and they go in that AAP's all.yml (docs/ENCLAVES.md) |
| `aap_template_audit_per_template` | `[report_email_to, report_email_cc, report_email_also, site_fail_on, target]` | Settings that belong in a template (who gets its report, what it runs on): never flagged as site-wide or as an address - still flagged when they are a secret, or the same in many templates |
| `aap_template_audit_ignore` | `[]` | settings never flagged |
| `aap_template_audit_ca_path` | (empty) | a CA file for AAP's HTTPS certificate ("" = what the execution environment trusts) |
| `aap_template_audit_fail` | `false` | true = the job fails when something is flagged or a part was not read (for a workflow's ticket step) |

## ad_lockout

File: `roles/ad_lockout/defaults/main.yml`

> Account lockout (playbooks/ad_lockout.yml): is the account locked out, and WHAT is locking it out - the computers its bad passwords came from, from the Security log of every domain controller. Read-only, unless ad_lockout_unlock. A PowerShell script on every DC (WinRM, the Windows Machine credential): the account needs to read the DCs' Security logs - see docs/ACTIVE_DIRECTORY.md, "Account lockout".

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ad_lockout_user` | (empty) | The account to look at, as the service desk is given it: jdoe, CORP\jdoe or jdoe@corp.example.mil (a survey question, NOT required). Several: one per line, or separated by commas. "" = every account locked out now, each with the computer locking it out. |
| `ad_lockout_hours` | `24` | the Security log entries of the last this-many hours (raise it for a lockout of last week) |
| `ad_lockout_max_users` | `25` | at most this many accounts (asked for, or locked out now) in one run |
| `ad_lockout_unlock` | `false` | true = unlock the account (on the PDC emulator) after reading - only an account asked for by name, and only when it is locked out. A dry run (Check) says what it would unlock. It locks out again as soon as the source computer tries its old password again: the report says what to fix first. |
| `ad_lockout_check_sources` | `false` | true = also look on each source computer that is a host of this job's inventory (Windows, WinRM, the same credential - it needs administrator rights there): services and scheduled tasks running as the account, its sessions (a disconnected Remote Desktop session), processes and mapped drives. Read-only. |
| `ad_lockout_check_max` | `5` | look on at most this many source computers per account (the worst first) |
| `ad_lockout_exchange_servers` | `[]` | Your mail servers (Exchange / ActiveSync, by name or address, * and ? allowed, e.g. [EXCH*, 192.0.2.25]): bad passwords coming through one of them are a phone or a mail app with the old password. |
| `ad_lockout_max_events` | `2000` | ---- How much is read ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ read at most this many Security log entries per account and DC (the newest) |
| `ad_lockout_resolve_max` | `50` | resolve at most this many addresses to names per DC (reverse DNS) |
| `ad_lockout_max_rows` | `50` | rows per table; the job's artifacts (ad_lockout) have all |

## ad_report

File: `roles/ad_report/defaults/main.yml`

> Active Directory health report (playbooks/ad_health_report.yml). Read-only: a PowerShell script on every domain controller (WinRM, the Windows Machine credential) and one more on one DC per domain - the account needs to read AD and run dcdiag / repadmin on the DCs; or, with no such account, reader mode from the AAP side as a plain domain user (ad_health_mode). See docs/ACTIVE_DIRECTORY.md.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `ad_health_mode` | `auto` | ---- Mode (1.4.0) ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- admin: a PowerShell script on every DC over WinRM (an account that may log on to the DCs, Domain Admins). reader: no WinRM - read from the AAP side over LDAP, DNS and Kerberos as a plain domain user with nothing granted;… (all of it: the role file) |
| `ad_reader_domain` | (empty) | ---- Reader mode ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- the AD domain's DNS name ("" = learned: the DCs' names, their ansible_host, their rootDSE, the EE's DNS search domain) |
| `ad_reader_user` | (empty) | "" = the job's Machine credential (UPN svc@CORP.EXAMPLE.MIL, CORP\svc, or a DN) |
| `ad_reader_password` | (empty) | "" = the Machine credential's (a simple bind over LDAPS, else StartTLS on 389 - never in clear) |
| `ad_reader_validate_certs` | `true` | the LDAPS / StartTLS certificate must be trusted and name the DC before the password is sent |
| `ad_reader_ca_file` | (empty) | a CA file ("" = what the execution environment trusts: ee/*/ca) |
| `ad_reader_kerberos` | `auto` | auto: a TGT from each KDC with kinit (the Windows EE has it), else an AS-REQ; tgt; probe (AS-REQ only); off |
| `ad_reader_dns_servers` | `[]` | DNS servers asked for the SRV and A records ([] = the execution environment's) |
| `ad_reader_ports` | `{ldap: 389, ldaps: 636, kerberos: 88, dns: 53}` | the ports the DCs answer on, and the DNS servers' |

## api_availability

File: `roles/api_availability/defaults/main.yml`

> AVAILABILITY CHECKS (playbooks/stigman_availability.yml, playbooks/servicenow_availability.yml): every 5 to 15 minutes, each address of the service asked a few times, read-only. A clean run is one line - no email. The job FAILS when the service is down (availability_fail_on), for a workflow's notification or ServiceNow ticket step; its own runs in AAP then give the availability over a day, a week and a month. docs/AVAILABILITY.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `availability_attempts` | `3` | times each address is asked in one run |
| `availability_pause_seconds` | `2` | seconds between two tries of one address |
| `availability_timeout` | `10` | seconds a try may take; no answer by then = a bad try |
| `availability_slow_ms` | `3000` | an answer slower than this (median of the tries), in milliseconds -> warning |
| `availability_node_down` | `warning` | One node (one server behind the service's address) that does not answer while the address still does: warning, or critical to fail the job for it too, or low (listed as Low: the service reads up). Every node down with no service address set: critical. |
| `availability_fail_on` | `[critical]` | The job shows FAILED (a workflow's "On failure" path) when a run finds a condition of these severities. |
| `availability_report_on` | `[critical]` | The report is emailed (report_email_to) and published (report_web_dest) only when a run finds a condition of these severities - [critical, warning] also for slow, flaky or one node down; a clean run is one line in the job output. |
| `availability_report_recovery` | `true` | also a report when the service answers again after a failed run ("UP again") |
| `availability_history` | `true` | The availability over these periods (hours), from this template's own runs in AAP: a run that ended well = up, a failed one = down. Needs a "Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform" credential on the template (Organization Auditor); without one the check still runs, without the percentages. |
| `availability_history_hours` | `[24, 168, 720]` | the periods: a day, a week, a month |

## cert_inventory

File: `roles/cert_inventory/defaults/main.yml`

> CERTIFICATE INVENTORY: every certificate report (Linux, Windows, VMware, network devices) can also write what it found - every certificate, with the same fields from each - for a dashboard (Power BI ...). Two ways, each on by itself: files (CSV + JSON) and a SQL Server table. A Check run writes nothing. The fields: id, source, host, location, subject, issuer, sans, not_after, days, status, tier (root / intermediate / ca-signed / self-signed), trust_store, in_use, public_key, sig_alg, serial, sha1, sha256, scanned_at, job (docs/CERT_INVENTORY.md).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `cert_inventory_files` | `false` | ---- files: <source>-certificates.csv and .json (source: linux, windows, vmware, net), replaced each run ---- true = write the files |
| `cert_inventory_dir` | `/var/lib/site-automation/cert-inventory` | where: on the AAP node the job runs on (a path AAP exposes to jobs: docs/CERT_INVENTORY.md), or on cert_inventory_host |
| `cert_inventory_host` | (empty) | an inventory host to write them on instead (a file server, or a Linux host with the share mounted); its credential must be on the job template |
| `cert_inventory_history` | `false` | true = also a dated copy (<source>-certificates-YYYY-MM-DD.csv) next to them, for trends |
| `cert_inventory_sql` | `false` | The login comes from the "SQL Server (certificate inventory)" credential (aap/credential_types/cert_inventory_sql.yml). The execution environment needs pymssql and community.general (the all-in-one EE has both). true = add / update the rows |
| `cert_inventory_sql_server` | (empty) | the SQL Server (name or address) |
| `cert_inventory_sql_port` | `1433` | its port |
| `cert_inventory_sql_database` | (empty) | the database (SQL Server 2016 or later: the rows go in as JSON, OPENJSON) |
| `cert_inventory_sql_table` | `dbo.cert_inventory` | schema.table |
| `cert_inventory_sql_create` | `false` | true = create the table (and its view <table>_current) when it is not there - the account then needs CREATE TABLE |

## check_auditd

File: `roles/check_auditd/defaults/main.yml`

> AUDITD: the audit system records who did what (the STIG depends on it). Running, enabled in the kernel, rules loaded, no events lost, room for its log, and (optionally) forwarding. Also how MUCH it records: too much rotates the evidence away within hours, fills the disk (then auditd stops the host or puts it in single-user mode, as the STIG sets it up), drops records on the way to the SIEM, and uses up the SIEM licence.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_auditd_min_rules` | `5` | fewer loaded rules than this = the STIG rules are missing |
| `check_auditd_log_warn_pct` | `75` | the audit log's filesystem |
| `check_auditd_log_crit_pct` | `90` | % used of that filesystem -> critical (warning from check_auditd_log_warn_pct) |
| `check_auditd_remote_required` | `false` | true = au-remote (audisp-remote) must be active |
| `check_auditd_exclude_accounts` | `[]` | Accounts whose audit events are expected in bulk and do NOT count toward the volume warning, e.g. the account a vulnerability scanner logs in with (a credentialed scan runs thousands of commands with sudo). Names or UIDs; a host that does not have the account skips it. The report still says how much they made, and the… (all of it: the role file) |
| `check_auditd_volume_hours` | `24` | look at the audit records of the last N hours |
| `check_auditd_volume_warn_mb_day` | `200` | warning above this many MB of audit records a day (excluded accounts not counted) |
| `check_auditd_retention_warn_hours` | `24` | With max_log_file_action ROTATE, auditd keeps num_logs files of max_log_file MB and deletes the oldest. Warning when what is left on disk reaches back fewer hours than this. The STIG wants a week (168) when the records are NOT sent off the host as they are written (RHEL-08-030660). 0 = off. |
| `check_auditd_volume_timeout` | `120` | The breakdown (which account, which rule, which program) reads the audit log files of the window at low CPU and disk priority, and only when the volume or the retention is over its limit. It stops after this many seconds on a host with very large logs (and says so). |

## check_containers

File: `roles/check_containers/defaults/main.yml`

> CONTAINERS: the podman containers on the host - root's (rootful) and every user's (rootless) - found by themselves (roles/podman_discover: which ones exist, which systemd unit runs each one, which should be running). Read-only. Which containers and users are looked at, and which are left out: the podman_discover_* settings.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_containers_required` | `[]` | Containers that MUST exist and run on these hosts: a container name, or OWNER/NAME for one owner (root/web, alice/web). A name alone matches that container of any owner. Also matches a Quadlet file name without .container, e.g. [stigman-mysql, stigman-api, alice/web]. |
| `check_containers_recent_hours` | `24` | A container that stopped with an error (exit code not 0) this many hours ago or less is reported (containers:crashed). Older crashes are history and are not reported. |
| `check_containers_restart_warn` | `3` | More restarts than this (podman's restart count, or its systemd unit's) = a restart loop. |

## check_disk

File: `roles/check_disk/defaults/main.yml`

> DISK: how full each LOCAL filesystem is (space and inodes), and - from the history of earlier runs - how many days until it is full. Network filesystems (NFS) are the mounts check's job: a hung NFS server can make `df` hang, so this check never touches them.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_disk_warn_pct` | `85` | % used -> warning |
| `check_disk_crit_pct` | `95` | % used -> critical |
| `check_disk_inode_warn_pct` | `85` | inodes: too many small files fill a disk too |
| `check_disk_inode_crit_pct` | `95` | % of inodes used -> critical (warning from check_disk_inode_warn_pct) |
| `check_disk_overrides` | `{}` | Different limits for particular mount points, e.g. keep the audit log partition emptier: check_disk_overrides: /var/log/audit: {warn: 70, crit: 85} |

## check_sso

File: `roles/check_sso/defaults/main.yml`

> SSO (read-only): can domain users still log in? A Linux host joined to Active Directory or IdM (sssd, realmd, winbind) keeps working on cached logins for a while after it loses its domain - then logins fail. A host that is not joined to any domain is skipped.

| `check_sso_kdc_warn` | `3` | "cannot contact any KDC" this many times -> warning |
| `check_sso_keytab` | `/etc/krb5.keytab` | the host's keytab |
| `check_sso_keytab_test` | `true` | get a ticket with it (kinit -k into memory: nothing is written) - proves the machine account works |
| `check_sso_testjoin` | `true` | adcli testjoin on hosts joined to Active Directory with adcli / realmd |
| `check_sso_test_users` | `[]` | domain users that must resolve (getent passwd), e.g. [svc_monitor@example.mil]; empty = none |
| `check_sso_sssd_dir` | `/etc/sssd` | sssd's configuration (sssd.conf, conf.d/): there = sssd is set up |
| `check_sso_smb_conf` | `/etc/samba/smb.conf` | Samba's: security = ads there = winbind is set up for Active Directory |
| `check_sso_sssd_log_dir` | `/var/log/sssd` | sssd's own logs, read with the journal |
| `check_sso_timeout` | `30` | seconds for each command that asks the domain (kinit, adcli, getent) |

## check_time

File: `roles/check_time/defaults/main.yml`

> TIME: is the clock synchronized, and by how much is it off? A clock that is off by minutes breaks Kerberos/AD logins (5 minutes), TLS, log correlation and audit evidence.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `check_time_offset_warn` | `0.5` | seconds |
| `check_time_offset_crit` | `5.0` | seconds off -> critical (warning from check_time_offset_warn) |
| `check_time_min_sources` | `1` | time servers chrony must be able to reach |

## check_trust

File: `roles/check_trust/defaults/main.yml`

> TRUST (read-only): which trust stores on the host still hold a certificate authority that was compromised or that the browsers dropped - the system bundles, p11-kit's live view and blocklist, Java cacerts, Python's certifi bundles, Node's built-in roots, the bundles inside running podman containers, certificate files an application carries - and the software with its own trust logic (Go programs, Node, NSS) below the version that fixed it. The list of certificates to look for ships with the check (roles/check_trust/vars/main.yml: October 2026, the eight eMudhra intermediates and their roots); add your own in check_trust_extra. The health check runs it in the weekly set; playbooks/trust_report.yml runs it on every host, vCenter and ESXi too.

|---|---|---|

Get the fingerprints with: openssl x509 -in the.pem -noout -fingerprint -sha256… (all of it: the role file) |
| `check_trust_severity` | `{}` | another severity for a listed name: {"AAA Certificate Services": warning} once you decide to blocklist it; notice (or low) = listed only, no finding, shown as Low |

| `check_trust_blocklist_dirs` | `[/etc/pki/ca-trust/source/blocklist, /usr/share/pki/ca-trust-source/blocklist]` | p11-kit blocklist folders: a certificate there is distrusted (listed as blocked, no finding) |

Left out on purpose: states that pass by themselves (being made, customized, deleted, waiting for the agent at start-up, maintenance). |

## incident_docs

File: `roles/incident_docs/defaults/main.yml`

> OUTAGE AAR AND SOP - WORD DOCUMENTS (playbooks/incident_aar.yml, playbooks/incident_sop.yml; docs/INCIDENT_DOCS.md). What is typed in the job's survey becomes an after action report (AAR.docx) - and, when asked, an SOP - with the site's logo (report_logo_file) and marking banner, emailed to the addresses typed in the survey (report_email_also). Never on the report website. The survey itself: the job "AAP - incident document surveys" writes it (playbooks/incident_docs_survey.yml).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `incident_docs_banner` | `auto` | The marking at the top and bottom of every page: auto = the reports' banner (report_banner_text, in its colour) when that banner is on - the classified enclave, or report_banner true (docs/ENCLAVES.md) - else CONTROLLED UNCLASSIFIED INFORMATION (CUI); your own text wins as it is; "" = none. |
| `incident_docs_banner_color` | (empty) | Its colour (bold text): "" = the marking's usual one - CUI purple (502B85), UNCLASSIFIED green (007A33), CONFIDENTIAL blue (0033A0), SECRET red (C8102E), TOP SECRET orange (FF8C00) - or, with auto, the reports' banner's; or your own, hex RRGGBB in quotes. |
| `incident_docs_logo_file` | (empty) | The logo at the top of the first page: report_logo_file, the reports' logo, unless this names another file (files/aar_logo.png = playbooks/files/aar_logo.png, in YOUR repository). "" = report_logo_file. |
| `incident_docs_logo_height` | `64` | pixels (its width follows) |
| `incident_docs_font` | `Times New Roman` | the documents' font |
| `incident_docs_font_size` | `12` | points |
| `incident_docs_heading_color` | `"1F2D86"` | the headings' colour (hex RRGGBB, in quotes) - dark blue |
| `incident_aar_instructions` | `- Save this file as AAR.docx. - Send it to your manager for review and approval before it…` | The site's own instructions at the end of each document, a numbered list (your all.yml: your teams' names and steps). [] = none. |
| `incident_sop_instructions` | `[]` | the same at the end of the SOP; [] = none |
| `incident_sop_status` | `Draft - review before use` | the SOP's Status line |
| `incident_docs_aar_file` | `AAR` | The attachments' names: AAR.docx (AAR-<outage>.docx when the outage is named), SOP-<title>.docx. the AAR attachment's first part |
| `incident_docs_sop_file` | `SOP` | the SOP attachment's first part |
| `incident_impact_levels` | `[MINOR, MODERATE, MAJOR, CRITICAL]` | The impact levels the survey offers (the setup job writes them into the survey). |
| `incident_docs_email_to` | `[]` | Who gets the documents: the addresses typed in the survey (report_email_also - held to report_email_also_domains when that is set), plus these. The reports' usual recipients (report_email_to) are NOT used here: an AAR goes only where it is sent. Nor is report_email_cc. |
| `incident_sop_draft_clear` | `true` | The SOP job empties the draft the AAR job put in its form (incident_sop_draft) once it made the SOP from it - only when launched with that draft's outage. Needs the AAP credential on the SOP template (incident_docs_draft_credential). |
| `incident_name` | (empty) | What was typed: the jobs' surveys ask these (the setup job writes the questions); empty unless answered. The AAR's boxes and the SOP's steps take a line or several. the outage's name or number (in the file name and the email) |
| `incident_start` | (empty) | the AAR: its start date and time (required) |
| `incident_end` | (empty) | its end date and time (optional) |
| `incident_impact_level` | (empty) | one of incident_impact_levels |
| `incident_impact` | (empty) | why: "it is affecting users enterprise-wide" |
| `incident_detection` | (empty) | how the event was detected |
| `incident_actions` | (empty) | key response steps and the teams involved |
| `incident_root_cause` | (empty) | the reason for the outage (RFO) |
| `incident_recovery` | (empty) | the fix action |
| `incident_successes` | (empty) | what went well |
| `incident_improvements` | (empty) | areas to improve |
| `incident_tasks` | (empty) | the improvements as tasks, each with who does it |
| `incident_make_sop` | `"No"` | Yes = the AAR job attaches an SOP too: a sop_ step box left empty = the AAR's Actions / Recovery |
| `incident_sop_draft` | `"No"` | Yes = the AAR job fills in the SOP job's survey from the AAR, to review and launch |
| `sop_title` | (empty) | the SOP's title |
| `sop_purpose` | (empty) | the symptoms that send someone to the SOP |
| `sop_troubleshoot` | (empty) | the steps to troubleshoot, one per line |
| `sop_fix` | (empty) | the steps to fix, one per line |
| `sop_verify` | (empty) | how to check it is fixed, one per line |
| `sop_escalate` | (empty) | who to call when the steps do not fix it |
| `incident_act_tidy` | `false` | ACT (GenAI, evidence mode: it runs no command, only reads what was typed). Each is a Yes/No in the survey; these are the defaults when the survey does not ask. Needs the "ACT model key" credential on the template when either is Yes. tidy the spelling and wording; facts, names and numbers stay as typed |
| `incident_act_suggest` | `false` | a "From ACT" section: what may be missing or better, to review |
| `incident_act_sop` | `false` | the AAR job's SOP: ACT writes the empty step boxes from the AAR's Actions and Recovery |
| `incident_act_max_suggestions` | `8` | suggestions from ACT at most |
| `incident_act_extra_instructions` | (empty) | the site's own words for ACT, e.g. "Our monitoring tool is called X." |
| `incident_act_model_timeout` | `120` | seconds GenAI may take to answer |
| `incident_docs_survey_state` | `present` | The survey setup job (playbooks/incident_docs_survey.yml): adds the questions to the job templates that run incident_aar.yml and incident_sop.yml (found by their playbook). A question already there is left as it is. present = add the questions; absent = take them out again |
| `incident_docs_survey_project` | (empty) | only job templates of this AAP project (its name); empty = any project |
| `incident_docs_survey_ca_path` | (empty) | a CA file for AAP's HTTPS certificate ("" = what the execution environment trusts) |
| `incident_docs_survey_max` | `8000` | characters a text box takes at most (AAP's own default is 1024) |
| `incident_docs_draft_credential` | (empty) | The SOP draft (incident_sop_draft) is written through AAP's API by the AAR job: name a "Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform" credential here and the setup job attaches it to the AAR and SOP templates (its user: Admin on the SOP template). Empty = attach it by hand, or no draft. |

## log_analysis

File: `roles/log_analysis/defaults/main.yml`

> LOG ANALYSIS (playbooks/log_analysis.yml for a group of servers, playbooks/vm_log_analysis.yml for vCenter and its ESXi hosts through vCenter's API). Read-only: each host's warning, error and critical log lines of the window, grouped on the AAP side into patterns (the same line with other numbers, times and names is one pattern, counted across hosts), and ACT (GenAI) explains the top ones - likely cause, evidence, fix, confidence - in evidence mode: ACT runs no command anywhere. Every setting can be set for all hosts, per group or host in the inventory, on the template, or as a survey answer (a list may be typed as "a, b" or one per line). docs/LOG_ANALYSIS.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `log_analysis_hours` | `24` | ---- the window ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ The last this-many hours ... |
| `log_analysis_since` | (empty) | ... or a fixed window, e.g. the outage: log_analysis_since "2026-10-23 08:00" and log_analysis_until "2026-10-23 10:30" - in UTC, also with report_time_zone set (the report shows the window in that zone and in UTC). Since alone = from then until now. |
| `log_analysis_until` | (empty) | the end of the fixed window (empty = now) |
| `log_analysis_source` | `auto` | ---- what to read ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ What a host is: auto (Windows when its connection is WinRM / PSRP, else Linux), linux, windows, or vcsa (a vCenter appliance over SSH: Linux, with the vcsa profile on). Set it per group in the inventory. |
| `log_analysis_profiles` | `[]` | Profiles: one word switches on the logs of a product (roles/log_analysis/vars/main.yml): vcsa, mid_server, iis, sql_server, nginx, httpd, mariadb, podman, sssd, idm, auditd, aap. E.g. for a group of web servers: log_analysis_profiles: [nginx, sssd] |
| `log_analysis_profiles_extra` | `{}` | Your own profiles, or a shipped one changed (the same name replaces it), the shape of vars/main.yml: log_analysis_profiles_extra: {stigman: {files: [/opt/stigman/logs/*.log], units: [stigman-api]}} |
| `log_analysis_priority` | `err` | Linux (and the vCenter appliance): the journal's lines of this priority or worse (journalctl -p: emerg, alert, crit, err, warning, notice). |
| `log_analysis_journal` | `true` | false = no journal (text logs, units and containers only) |
| `log_analysis_units` | `[]` | Units and syslog identifiers whose journal is read at log_analysis_units_priority, lower than the rest: e.g. [sssd, nginx, stigman-api] (globs such as dirsrv@* work) and [sudo, sshd]. |
| `log_analysis_identifiers` | `[]` | syslog identifiers read the same way, e.g. [sudo, sshd] |
| `log_analysis_units_priority` | `warning` | the priority those units and identifiers are read at |
| `log_analysis_containers` | `[]` | Podman containers whose output (podman logs) of the window is read, its lines that match log_analysis_match: a name for root's, user/name for a user's (rootless), e.g. [stigman-api, svc_app/web]. |
| `log_analysis_files` | `[]` | Text logs (globs), read when they changed in the window: their matching lines, the newest log_analysis_max_lines. Compressed rotations (.gz .xz .bz2 .zst) are left out. log_analysis_files is the base list; log_analysis_files_extra adds to it and to the profiles' files (never replaces them). e.g. [/var/log/messages, /v… (all of it: the role file) |
| `log_analysis_files_extra` | `[]` | e.g. [/opt/app/logs/*.log] |
| `log_analysis_become` | `true` | read as root (sudo), as the other checks do |
| `log_analysis_win_logs` | `[System, Application]` | Windows: the event logs read, their critical (1), error (2) and - log_analysis_win_level 3 - warning events. |
| `log_analysis_win_logs_extra` | `[]` | more channels, e.g. ["Microsoft-Windows-TaskScheduler/Operational", "Directory Service", "DNS Server"] |
| `log_analysis_win_level` | `3` | 1 critical, 2 + error, 3 + warning |
| `log_analysis_win_providers` | `[]` | Event providers whose events are read at every level up to information, in the logs above (e.g. [Service Control Manager]); log_analysis_win_providers_only: true = only these providers' events. |
| `log_analysis_win_providers_only` | `false` | true = only those providers' events |
| `log_analysis_win_event_ids` | `[]` | Event IDs always read whatever their level: "Log:ID", or a number for every log read plus Security, e.g. [4625, 4740, "System:7031", "System:7034"]. Security needs an account that may read it. |
| `log_analysis_win_files` | `[]` | Text logs (wildcards), read like the Linux ones; _extra adds to the base list and the profiles', e.g. ['D:\Apps\*\logs\*.log'] (a MID Server's agent logs: the mid_server profile) |
| `log_analysis_win_files_extra` | `[]` | more Windows text logs, added to the list above |
| `log_analysis_match` | `"error\|fail\|fatal\|crit\|panic\|denied\|refused\|timed out\|timeout\|unable to\|cannot\|exception\|…` | The words that make a line of a text log or a container's output worth reading (grep -E, any case); _extra adds words, e.g. [SEVERE, 'HTTP/1.1" 5']. |
| `log_analysis_match_extra` | `[]` | more words, added to log_analysis_match |
| `log_analysis_vcenter_logs` | `[vpxd]` | ---- vCenter and ESXi through vCenter's API (playbooks/vm_log_analysis.yml) ------------------------ No SSH and no login to the hosts: vCenter hands over its own logs and each host's (the "VMware vCenter" credential; a read-only role plus Global > Diagnostics). Keys as vCenter names them. [] = not vCenter's own log |

| `log_analysis_max_chars` | `60000` | the evidence ACT reads is cut at this many characters |
| `log_analysis_check_url` | `true` | first check that the AAP node can reach the model's URL |

A run that finds nothing is not emailed unless log_analys… (all of it: the role file) |
| `log_analysis_max_rows` | `200` | rows per table in the report (the artifacts have them all) |

## mail_relay

File: `roles/mail_relay/defaults/main.yml`

> MAIL RELAY WHITELIST, with an approval: add IP addresses or subnets to the list of clients the mail relay lets relay - with a comment saying who or what they are for - or remove them. The plan job (playbooks/mail_relay_plan.yml) checks the request, reads the list on every relay server and emails what would change - "waiting for approval"; it changes nothing. After a person approves in AAP, the approved job (playbooks/mail_relay_approved.yml) writes exactly that (the file backed up first), checks the mail configuration and that Postfix reads the list as written, reloads Postfix and emails the result; a failed check puts the file back. The format job (playbooks/mail_relay_format.yml) puts each relay's list one address or subnet per line - subnets first, then the single addresses, in number order - each single address with a comment line above it: its name in DNS (looked up on the relay) and the folder the VM that has it is in, in vCenter ("# web01.example.mil Payroll [AAP]"); the list keeps exactly its addresses, a copy of main.cf is kept first. The unused job (playbooks/mail_relay_unused.yml) reads each relay's mail logs and plans the removal of the addresses that sent no mail in mail_relay_unused_days - the same approval and apply step as a removal. docs/MAIL_RELAY.md

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `mail_relay_action` | (empty) | ---- The request (a survey on the workflow) ----------------------------------------------------- add or remove: set in each workflow's Variables (one workflow per action) |
| `mail_relay_ip` | (empty) | one address (198.51.100.3), a subnet (198.51.100.0/24), or several separated by commas: "198.51.100.3, 198.51.100.4" |
| `mail_relay_comment` | (empty) | add: required - the name and/or service the addresses are for, e.g. "Payroll app (svc-payroll)". Written above the mynetworks line, one line per address: "# 198.51.100.3 Payroll app (svc-payroll) [added 2026-10-22 by jdoe]" |
| `mail_relay_requested_by` | (empty) | who asked (e.g. sent by Orchestrator); "" = the AAP user who launched it |
| `mail_relay_group` | `mail_relays` | ---- The relay servers and their list ----------------------------------------------------------- the inventory group of the mail relay servers: every one is changed |
| `mail_relay_style` | `main_cf` | main_cf: the list is the mynetworks line of Postfix's main.cf ("mynetworks = 127.0.0.0/8, 192.0.2.10"); an address is added at the end of the line (", 198.51.100.3"). file: a list file with one address per line (mynetworks = /etc/postfix/mynetworks, or a Postfix access map), its comment on the line above it. |
| `mail_relay_file` | `/etc/postfix/main.cf` | the file with the list on each relay (a relay's own host_vars may differ) |
| `mail_relay_parameter` | `mynetworks` | main_cf: the parameter that holds the list |
| `mail_relay_postconf` | `postconf` | main_cf: after a change, read the list back as Postfix does ("" = do not) |
| `mail_relay_entry_suffix` | (empty) | file: after the address on its line: " OK" for a Postfix access map |
| `mail_relay_postmap` | `false` | file: true = run postmap on the file after a change (a hash: or lmdb: map) |
| `mail_relay_check_command` | `postfix check` | run after a change; when it fails the file is put back ("" = no check) |
| `mail_relay_reload_service` | `postfix` | reloaded after a change ("" = no reload) |
| `mail_relay_become` | `true` | change the file as root (sudo) |
| `mail_relay_allow_subnets` | `true` | ---- What a request may ask for ----------------------------------------------------------------- a subnet (198.51.100.0/24) too; false = single addresses only |
| `mail_relay_min_prefix` | `24` | the widest subnet accepted (/24 = 256 addresses); 0.0.0.0/0 and the like never |
| `mail_relay_max_ips` | `20` | the most addresses in one request |
| `mail_relay_comment_min` | `3` | the comment's least characters |
| `mail_relay_comment_max` | `200` | the comment's most characters |
| `mail_relay_format_dns` | `true` | ---- The format job (playbooks/mail_relay_format.yml) ----------------------------------------- look up each single address's name on the relay (getent hosts: DNS, /etc/hosts) |
| `mail_relay_format_dns_timeout` | `5` | seconds for one lookup |
| `mail_relay_format_vmware` | `true` | find the VM that has the address (needs the "VMware vCenter" credential) |
| `mail_relay_format_blank_lines` | `true` | a blank line between the single addresses (Postfix skips it) |
| `mail_relay_format_refresh` | `false` | true = look up again the addresses this job named before (others kept) |
| `mail_relay_format_reload` | `false` | true = reload Postfix after (the list is the same: no need) |
| `mail_relay_format_check_email` | `true` | a dry run (Check) emails its report too, marked DRY RUN (false = only printed) |
| `mail_relay_unused_days` | `183` | ---- The unused addresses (playbooks/mail_relay_unused.yml: workflow "Mail relay - remove unused addresses") ------ an address that sent no mail through any relay in this many days is unused (183: six months) |
| `mail_relay_unused_logs` | `["/var/log/maillog*"]` | Postfix's log files on each relay (patterns; rotated and .gz copies too; a folder - /var/log/maillog_archive: every file in it and its folders) |
| `mail_relay_unused_journal` | `auto` | auto = read the journal when no log file is there; true = as well; false = never |
| `mail_relay_unused_keep` | `[]` | addresses or subnets never proposed, e.g. [198.51.100.7, 203.0.113.0/28] (127.0.0.0/8 never is) |
| `mail_relay_unused_max` | `50` | the most addresses one plan removes (the next run takes the rest) |
| `mail_relay_unused_accept_short_logs` | `false` | The logs must go back mail_relay_unused_days on every relay (RHEL keeps about 5 weeks of /var/log/maillog): else nothing is proposed. true = propose anyway, from what the logs cover (the email says how far back they go). |
| `mail_relay_approve_url` | (empty) | ---- The approval email ------------------------------------------------------------------------- Both emails (waiting for approval, and the result) go to report_email_to (set it on the workflow). A link for the approvers in the first one: your AAP's Workflow Approvals page, copied from the browser ("" = no link). |
| `mail_relay_web` | `false` | The report website (report_web_dest): the plan, the result and the format's report are emailed only; true = also published there, as the other reports (a website that cannot be written then fails the job before the approval). |

## net_certs

File: `roles/net_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> NETWORK DEVICE CERTIFICATES (playbooks/net_cert_report.yml, net_cert_renew.yml): the TLS certificate each switch, firewall, printer, iLO / iDRAC, UPS, storage ... presents, read from the controller with a TLS hello - no login to the devices, nothing changed. The renewal: a ServiceNow incident per certificate due; on a Cisco IOS / IOS-XE device, optionally a CSR made on the device (net_cert_cisco_csr).

| `net_cert_ports` | `[443]` | the ports read (a host's own net_cert_ports wins), e.g. [443, 8443, 636] |
| `net_cert_subnets` | `[]` | CIDR ranges to sweep (net_cert_targets: subnets or both), e.g. ['192.0.2.0/24'] - every address, each port in net_cert_ports |
| `net_cert_exclude` | `[]` | never connected to: addresses, CIDR ranges, host name patterns (e.g. ['192.0.2.1', 'ups*']) |
| `net_cert_max_addresses` | `4096` | a sweep bigger than this (all subnets together) is refused: a /16 by mistake would take hours |
| `net_cert_resolve_names` | `true` | a swept address that answers: its DNS name (PTR) in the report, else the address |
| `net_cert_timeout` | `5` | seconds for each connection, and each handshake |
| `net_cert_workers` | `32` | connections at the same time |
| `net_cert_only` | `[]` | only these devices (names, wildcards), e.g. ['sw01*'] - to try the renewal on one |
| `net_cert_warn_days` | `30` | ---- what is due ---- a certificate expiring within this many days is due: a warning incident (amber in the report) |
| `net_cert_crit_days` | `7` | within this many days (or expired): critical |
| `net_cert_notice_days` | `60` | the report shows these as Low (a heads-up, no incident) |
| `net_cert_unanswered_finding` | `false` | true = an inventory device whose port gives no certificate gets an incident too (a warning) |
| `net_cert_cisco_csr` | `false` | On: for a due certificate of an inventory host with ansible_network_os cisco.ios.ios (and its network_cli credential on the job template), the job makes a key on the device (crypto key generate rsa, not exportable), a trustpoint <prefix>-<expiry> (enrollment terminal) and its CSR (crypto pki enroll), and attaches the… (all of it: the role file) |
| `net_cert_cisco_key_bits` | `2048` | the new RSA key (2048, 3072, 4096) |
| `net_cert_cisco_trustpoint_prefix` | `SA-RENEW` | the trustpoint and key label: SA-RENEW-20270131 (the old certificate's expiry) |

## net_config

File: `roles/net_config/defaults/main.yml`

> NETWORK DEVICE CONFIGURATIONS: the backup (playbooks/net_config_backup.yml) keeps each device's running configuration - in a git repository (a commit when one changed) or on a file share (dated copies) - and can open a ServiceNow incident when one changed. The load (playbooks/net_config_load.yml) sends configuration lines, or restores a backup, after an approved change request - run it in Check first to see what it sends (the job does not check that you did: an approval step in a workflow does); a real load first keeps each device's running configuration (net_config_keep_before). Cisco IOS / IOS-XE (over its CLI: network_cli, a Machine credential) and Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (over its XML API from the controller: the "Palo Alto PAN-OS API" credential). docs/NETWORK_CONFIG.md. A backup holds the device's secrets (password hashes, SNMP communities, keys): keep it in a private, internal repository or share only - never in this one.

| `net_config_git_path` | `configs` | the folder in the repository: <path>/<device>.cfg (IOS), .xml (PAN-OS) |
| `net_config_git_author_name` | `site-automation` | the commits' author |
| `net_config_git_author_email` | `site-automation@localhost` | and its email |
| `net_config_git_host_key_checking` | `accept-new` | The git server's SSH host key: accept-new (the first connection learns it), or yes (only the keys in net_config_git_known_hosts - lines as in a known_hosts file). In an execution environment ssh's own known_hosts is empty every job, so accept-new learns the key each time: only net_config_git_known_hosts + yes really c… (all of it: the role file) |
| `net_config_git_known_hosts` | (empty) | the git server's host keys (known_hosts lines), for net_config_git_host_key_checking: yes |
| `net_config_share_dir` | `/var/lib/site-automation/net-config` | The folder for share: on the AAP node (a path AAP exposes to jobs) or on net_config_share_host - <dir>/<device>/<device>.cfg (the latest), and a dated copy beside it each time one changed. |
| `net_config_share_host` | (empty) | an inventory host to keep them on (Linux, or a Windows file server); its credential on the template |
| `net_config_share_keep` | `30` | dated copies kept per device (the oldest go) |
| `net_config_ios_command` | `show running-config` | ---- what is read ---- IOS: the command whose output is kept |
| `net_config_panos_port` | `443` | PAN-OS: the XML API's HTTPS port |

| `net_config_keep_before` | `true` | A real load first reads each device's running configuration and keeps it where the backup keeps them (net_config_store), named <time>-before-<change> (git: a tag; share: a dated copy) - restore it with net_config_load_mode: restore and net_config_restore_ref set to that name. A device whose copy could not be kept gets… (all of it: the role file) |

Read-only, except the few files of the host's own history (net_perf_dir). docs/NETWORK_PERF.md.

A target may also be set per group or host (net_perf_targets_extr… (all of it: the role file) |

| `net_perf_ocsp_warn_ms` | `2000` | an OCSP answer slower than this -> warning |

## servicenow

> SERVICENOW - open, update (and optionally resolve) incidents from check findings, and check that ServiceNow itself (the instance and its MID Servers) is healthy. Uses the REST Table API with ansible.builtin.uri: no extra collection to install. Connection: the "ServiceNow API" AAP credential sets SN_HOST (https://<instance>), SN_USERNAME and SN_PASSWORD in the job's environment. Without it, nothing is sent: the job prints what it WOULD have opened (a safe way to try it out).

## servicenow_insights

File: `roles/servicenow_insights/defaults/main.yml`

> TICKET INSIGHTS (playbooks/servicenow_insights.yml, docs/SERVICENOW_INSIGHTS.md): months of ServiceNow tickets in one report for management - the most common incident issues and their fix, the most requested services, keeping up (opened, resolved, the backlog and its age), P1/P2s, problem candidates, tickets passed between groups, changes that failed and what followed, close notes that say nothing, the All-stars of each team, knowledge article drafts. A web page for the whole site and one per team (report_web_dest), an email (report_email_to) with the workbook. ACT (GenAI) groups the incidents into issues and writes the fixes; names, phone numbers, email addresses, host names and IP addresses are replaced before anything reaches the model and put back after. From the AAP side with the "ServiceNow API" credential (the account needs read on the tables: itil). Read-only, in Check too.

Dates and weeks follow report_time_zone (the email settings; "" = UTC). |

## site_findings

File: `roles/site_findings/defaults/main.yml`

> Shared by every check playbook. A "finding" is one thing that is wrong on one host:   check:    the check that found it (disk, services, mariadb, ...)   id:       a stable name for this problem on this host, e.g. disk:/var. ServiceNow uses it to             update the same ticket instead of opening a new one every run.   severity: critical \| warning   summary:  one line a person understands ("/var is 96% full (critical at 95%)")   hint:     a read-only command that shows more. A person can paste it into a shell; ACT (when             you add it later) runs it to collect evidence. Check roles only ADD findings. This role starts the list, reports it, and decides pass/fail.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `site_fail_on` | `[critical, warning]` | Which severities make the job FAIL. A failed job is what sends an AAP workflow down its "on failure" path (open tickets, ask ACT, wait for approval). [] = report only, never fail. |
| `site_unreachable_fails` | `false` | A host that cannot be reached (switched off, no network, ssh or WinRM refused, its login refused) in the health checks, the certificate report and renewal, database health, the service watch and troubleshoot: listed as NOT REACHED and left out, and the job is not failed for it. It still counts as checked-for, so the S… (all of it: the role file) |
| `site_syslog` | `true` | One syslog line per finding (tag below), so your log server / SIEM sees them too. |
| `site_syslog_tag` | `site-health` | the syslog tag those lines carry (to filter on in the SIEM) |
| `site_eventlog_source` | `site-health` | Windows: one Application event log entry per finding instead of syslog (source below). |
| `site_os` | `linux` | ---- Linux or Windows (set by the playbook; do not set) ----------------------------------------- Linux playbooks run the roles check_<name>, the Windows ones (win_*.yml) the roles win_check_<name>. |
| `site_check_role_prefix` | `"{{ 'win_check_' if site_os == 'windows' else 'check_' }}"` | check_ (Linux) or win_check_ (Windows): set by the playbook from site_os |
| `site_windows_connections` | `[winrm, psrp, ansible.builtin.winrm, ansible.builtin.psrp]` | How a host is recognized as Windows: its connection, or its shell (Windows OpenSSH). |
| `site_settings_notice` | `true` | A notice in the job output when a project settings file (playbooks/group_vars/*.yml) defines a setting: it wins over AAP's inventory Variables box. false = no notice. |
| `patch_age_groups` | `[]` | ---- Patch age (1.61.0): a section of the health reports ---------------------------------------- When the patching check ran: days since each host's last update, by host group. Late: Linux check_patching_max_age_days, Windows win_check_patching_warn_days (critical from win_check_patching_crit_days). Changes no findin… (all of it: the role file) |
| `patch_age_due_days` | `7` | due soon (Low) = late within this many days |

## tenable_scan

File: `roles/tenable_scan/defaults/main.yml`

> ACAS SCAN (playbooks/tenable_scan.yml, docs/TENABLE.md): kick off a Tenable.sc (ACAS) scan of the hosts of an inventory group, from the scanner of each host's own datacenter - Tenable.sc's scan zones say which scanners cover which IP ranges - one scan per zone. From the AAP side, with the "Tenable.sc API" credential. Nothing is launched without tenable_scan_policy and tenable_scan_repository: a first run lists the zones, scanners, policies and repositories the account may use. A dry run (Check) chooses the zones and says what it would launch.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `tenable_scan_target` | (empty) | The hosts: a group or pattern of this inventory (the job runs on localhost: not the Limit), and/or names or addresses not in the inventory. "" and [] = nothing to scan: the job lists what Tenable.sc offers. a group or pattern of the inventory (web_servers, dc1_*) |
| `tenable_scan_targets` | `[]` | names or addresses not in the inventory, e.g. [198.51.100.5, nas01.example.mil] |
| `tenable_scan_policy` | (empty) | the scan policy (name or id): the first run lists them |
| `tenable_scan_repository` | (empty) | the repository the results go to (name or id) |
| `tenable_scan_credentials` | `[]` | scan credentials (names or ids) the scans log in to the hosts with |
| `tenable_scan_name` | `"AAP {target} - {zone}"` | The scans' name: {target} = tenable_scan_target (or the number of hosts), {zone} = the zone. A scan of that name from an earlier run is updated (its hosts) and launched again, not made twice. |
| `tenable_scan_description` | `"Launched by site-automation (AAP), playbooks/tenable_scan.yml"` | the scans' description in Tenable.sc |
| `tenable_scan_sites` | `{}` | The zone (the scanners) of each host - the first rule that applies: 1. the host's own tenable_zone (an inventory variable: a zone's name) 2. its site, through tenable_scan_sites: a group of the host, or the site code tenable_scan_site_regex takes from its name, mapped to a zone's name - e.g. {dc_east: "Datacenter East… (all of it: the role file) |
| `tenable_scan_site_regex` | (empty) | e.g. '^([a-z]{2}[0-9])': the first group is the site code in the host's name (xy2vmp02 -> xy2) |
| `tenable_scan_zone_default` | (empty) | rule 4: a zone's name, auto, or "" (a host no rule gives a zone is not scanned) |
| `tenable_scan_wait` | `false` | true = wait for the scans and report the findings by severity and by host |
| `tenable_scan_wait_minutes` | `120` | at most this long |
| `tenable_scan_poll_seconds` | `60` | seconds between two looks at a running scan |
| `tenable_scan_max_targets` | `256` | at most this many hosts per run (narrow tenable_scan_target, or raise it) |
| `tenable_scan_max_rows` | `200` | rows per table in the report |
| `tenable_scan_fail` | `true` | The job fails when Tenable.sc could not be read, a policy or repository named is not there, or a scan could not be launched. false = a report only. A host no rule gives a zone is said (amber), never a failure. |
| `tenable_ca_path` | (empty) | a CA file for Tenable.sc's HTTPS certificate ("" = what the execution environment trusts) |
| `tenable_timeout` | `60` | seconds per request |

## vmware_ask_stack

File: `roles/vmware_ask_stack/defaults/main.yml`

> VMware ask - the web page of "VM - ask a question" - one container on podman, managed by systemd through a Quadlet unit file: vmware-ask-app (the service: questions, GenAI through ACT, the vCenter reads). It sits behind the reverse proxy you have - STIG Manager's nginx, in its podman container - at /ask/: that nginx does TLS and the client certificates (mTLS, the CAC), and passes who it verified. The role joins the service to that nginx's podman network and writes the nginx lines to add (vmware_ask_config_dir/nginx-ask.conf); it never changes the nginx, its files, its network or any other container (docs/VMWARE_ASK.md). Needs podman >= 4.4 (Quadlet): RHEL 9.2+ / RHEL 8.8+.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `vmware_ask_scope` | `system` | system = rootful (/etc/containers/systemd, systemctl) <- production user = rootless (~/.config/containers/systemd, systemctl --user) <- tests / rootless hosts |
| `vmware_ask_image` | `aap.example.mil/site-ee-all:1` | the service's image: the site's execution environment (ee/all-in-one) - Python, ansible-core and pyVmomi are in it already, so nothing is installed on the server or downloaded at start. Pull it from your automation hub. |
| `vmware_ask_config_dir` | `/etc/vmware-ask` | the service's files, and nginx-ask.conf (the nginx lines to add) |
| `vmware_ask_network` | (empty) | the podman network of the reverse proxy's nginx container (required): `sudo podman ps --format "{{.Names}} {{.Networks}}"` shows it. It must exist with DNS on (a network you made, not podman's default "podman"); the service joins it, the role never creates or changes it |
| `vmware_ask_path` | `/ask/` | the page's path on the reverse proxy (nginx-ask.conf's location) |
| `vmware_ask_public_url` | `"https://{{ inventory_hostname }}{{ vmware_ask_path }}"` | the page's address, as people open it (said at the end, and logged) |
| `vmware_ask_title` | `Ask VMware` | the page's title |
| `vmware_ask_classification` | `U` | banner: U, CUI, C, S, TS, SCI, NONE |
| `vmware_ask_vcenters` | `"{{ vmware_vcenters \| default([]) }}"` | vCenter: the "VMware vCenter" credential's account (read-only is enough) and vCenter, and these vCenters with it more vCenters, the same account (as vmware_vcenters) |
| `vmware_ask_validate_certs` | `"{{ vmware_validate_certs \| default(true) }}"` | check vCenter's certificate (the CAs: vmware_ask_trust_host_cas) |
| `vmware_ask_datacenter` | (empty) | only this datacenter; "" = all |
| `vmware_ask_refresh_minutes` | `10` | read vCenter every this many minutes (the answers are as of the last read) |
| `vmware_ask_refresh_timeout` | `1800` | seconds one read may take |
| `vmware_ask_event_days` | `"{{ vm_ask_event_days \| default(30) }}"` | a VM's last power off, restart and vMotion: from vCenter's events of this many days |
| `vmware_ask_max_events` | `"{{ vm_ask_max_events \| default(50000) }}"` | at most this many of those events per vCenter |
| `vmware_ask_genai` | `true` | GenAI: ACT's settings (site_act_provider, site_act_models, site_act_urls ...: roles/site_act/defaults/main.yml) and the key of the "ACT model key" credential. No key: the job's own reader answers the simplest questions. false = only the job's own reader |
| `vmware_ask_local_fallback` | `"{{ vm_ask_local_fallback \| default(true) }}"` | GenAI did not run or gave no query: the job's own reader tries it (said) |
| `vmware_ask_genai_retry` | `"{{ vm_ask_genai_retry \| default(true) }}"` | GenAI's answer held no query: asked once more, told what it answered |
| `vmware_ask_model_timeout` | `"{{ vm_ask_model_timeout \| default(120) }}"` | seconds GenAI may take to answer |
| `vmware_ask_extra_instructions` | `"{{ vm_ask_extra_instructions \| default('') }}"` | more words for GenAI, e.g. your naming |
| `vmware_ask_max_rows` | `"{{ vm_ask_max_rows \| default(500) }}"` | rows shown on the page (the CSV has every row) |
| `vmware_ask_keep_days` | `365` | keep who asked what this many days (0 = for ever) |
| `vmware_ask_parallel` | `4` | questions with GenAI at once (the rest wait) |
| `vmware_ask_per_user` | `2` | questions one person may have running at once |
| `vmware_ask_trust_host_cas` | `true` | the service trusts what the server trusts (/etc/pki/ca-trust): vCenter, GenAI |
| `vmware_ask_ready_retries` | `30` | How long to wait after (re)starting for the service to answer |
| `vmware_ask_ready_delay` | `4` | seconds between those tries |
| `vmware_ask_vcenter_host` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'VMWARE_HOST') }}"` | ---- Secrets: NEVER set these in a vars file or inventory ----------------------------------- They come from AAP credentials as environment variables / files on the controller (execution environment). the "VMware vCenter" credential |
| `vmware_ask_vcenter_user` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'VMWARE_USER') }}"` | its account |
| `vmware_ask_vcenter_password` | `"{{ lookup('ansible.builtin.env', 'VMWARE_PASSWORD') }}"` | its password: a podman secret on the server |

## win_check_accounts

File: `roles/win_check_accounts/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS ACCOUNTS (local accounts; domain controllers have none and are skipped)   - the built-in Guest account is disabled                               -> critical if not   - enabled local accounts: password never expires, password too old,     no logon for a long time                                             -> warning   - members of the local Administrators group that you did not allow     -> warning Names below allow wildcards (* and ?), e.g. 'YOURDOMAIN\Domain Admins', '*\svc_aap'.

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_accounts_password_max_age_days` | `60` | an enabled local account's password older than this -> warning (0 = off) |

## win_check_certs

File: `roles/win_check_certs/defaults/main.yml`

> WINDOWS CERTIFICATES: every certificate in the machine stores below, and which of them are in use (https bindings of IIS / WSUS / ..., the WinRM HTTPS listener AAP connects through, Remote Desktop). Expiring soon -> warning / critical. Expired: critical when in use, or when it expired less than win_check_certs_expired_report_days ago (older leftovers are only listed in the certificate report).

| Setting | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `win_check_certs_warn_days` | `30` | a certificate expiring within this many days -> warning (amber in the certificate report) |
| `win_check_certs_notice_days` | `60` | the certificate report shows these as Low (an early heads-up; not a finding) |
| `win_check_certs_crit_days` | `7` | within this many days -> critical |
| `win_check_certs_expired_report_days` | `30` | an expired certificate NOT in use is a finding for this many days after it expired; older ones only in the report |
| `win_check_certs_stores` | `['Cert:\LocalMachine\My', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\WebHosting', 'Cert:\LocalMachine\Remote Des…` | the machine certificate stores read |
| `win_check_certs_trust` | `false` | also every other machine store: Trusted Root, Intermediate CAs, Other People, ... (the certificate report turns it on); with its private key checked as above, without it only listed (trust store) |
| `win_check_certs_trust_skip_stores` | `['Disallowed', 'AuthRoot', 'REQUEST', 'SMS']` | stores never read: the untrusted certificates, the roots Windows Update keeps, pending requests (a CSR's key), the MECM client's own |
| `win_check_certs_remote_desktop` | `false` | false = Remote Desktop's certificates are left out of the report and the renewal (Windows or the GPO renews them): the Remote Desktop store, the one RDP uses, those for Remote Desktop only; true = checked like the others |
| `win_check_certs_ignore_subjects` | `[]` | wildcards, e.g. ['CN=localhost*'] |
| `win_check_certs_endpoints` | `[]` | TLS services whose certificate a client actually gets, e.g. win_check_certs_endpoints: - {name: IIS, host: 127.0.0.1, port: 443, servername: web01.yoursite.mil} |
| `win_cert_renew_dir` | `'C:\ProgramData\site-automation\renew'` | ---- Renewal: a new key and CSR for each certificate that expires soon (playbooks/win_cert_renew_csr.yml) ---- The certificates the Windows certificate report flags (within win_check_certs_warn_days, or expired) that are the server's own - not a trust store's - get a new key and a CSR with the same subject, names and… (all of it: the role file) |
| `win_cert_renew_key_bits` | `2048` | RSA key size, at least 2048 (a bigger old key keeps its size; an EC certificate gets a new key on the same curve) |
| `win_cert_renew_digest` | `sha256` | the CSR's signature: sha256, sha384 or sha512 |
| `win_cert_renew_max` | `10` | at most this many NEW CSRs per server in one run (the rest come the next run) |
| `win_cert_renew_self_signed` | `false` | true = a self-signed certificate gets a CSR too, for the PKI to issue a real one in its place (never one only for localhost) |
| `win_cert_renew_issuer` | (empty) | regular expression: only certificates whose issuer matches (empty = any CA), e.g. 'O=U\.S\. Government' |
| `win_cert_renew_exclude_issuer` | (empty) | regular expression: certificates whose issuer matches are never renewed here (renewed by their own tool) |
| `win_cert_renew_only` | (empty) | regular expression on the certificate's place, e.g. 'used by https' (empty = every one) |
| `win_cert_renew_exportable` | `false` | true = the new key can be exported (to move it to another server); false keeps it on this one |
| `win_cert_install_rebind` | `[https, rdp, winrm]` | ---- Install: the issued certificate (playbooks/win_cert_install_check.yml -> approval -> playbooks/win_cert_install_approved.yml) ---- The PKI's certificate, from the request carrying the CSR (cert_renew_servicenow: catalog), is put together with its pending key by certreq -accept -machine (in Personal); its chain's… (all of it: the role file) |
| `win_cert_install_verify_wait` | `15` | seconds an https port has, after the rebinding, to serve the new certificate (full PowerShell only) |
| `win_cert_restore_backup` | (empty) | ---- Restore: the bindings back on the old certificate (playbooks/win_cert_restore.yml) ---- a backup's folder name, as the restore's Check lists it |
| `win_cert_restore_only` | (empty) | or: the newest backup of each certificate whose thumbprint or subject matches (a regular expression) |

## Settings of one host

Set these on the host itself: its host variables in the inventory, or the host's **Variables** box
in AAP. Never in a job template's Variables - there one value would be used for every host. When a
host has none, the role works the value out from the host, so no role file has a default for them.

| Setting | Role | When not set | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| `net_config_address` | [net_config](#net_config) | the host's `ansible_host`, else its name | The address the backup and load jobs connect to, when it is not `ansible_host` (PAN-OS) |
| `net_config_platform` | [net_config](#net_config) | from `ansible_network_os` | `ios` or `panos`: the platform of a host that has no `ansible_network_os` (`cisco.ios.ios` / `paloaltonetworks.panos`) |
| `net_cert_address` | [net_certs](#net_certs) | the host's `ansible_host`, else its name | The address the certificate report connects to (a host of `net_cert_group`) |
| `net_cert_servername` | [net_certs](#net_certs) | the host's name | The name sent in the TLS hello (SNI): the certificate a device with several names shows for this one |
| `servicenow_node_label` | [servicenow](#servicenow) | from `servicenow_node_labels`, else the host's short name | The friendly name of one self-hosted node in the health report ("Node 1"), set on that node's host |
